title: The corpus taught the 1958 Act's 'formal investigation' as current 2025 casualty machinery
candidate_claim: GPT review pass 2A found that candidate-facing cards present the Indian casualty machinery as 'report -> preliminary inquiry -> formal investigation before a court with assessors, with powers over officers' certificates', attributed to the Merchant Shipping Act 2025, and authorised its replacement with the current structure at four named sites.
candidate_verdict: UPHELD, AND WIDER THAN THE FOUR SITES NAMED. 'Formal investigation' occurs ZERO times in the Merchant Shipping Act 2025. The authorisation enumerated four locations; the corpus carried the same mapping in twelve candidate-facing places across six files, and the brief's own named content gate - 'no candidate-facing MS Act 2025 claim still says casualty formal investigation' - is unsatisfiable unless all of them move. Section 13 of the brief lists 'same stale formal investigation legal mapping' as ALLOWED propagation, which is the authority relied on for the additional sites. This is a SUBSTANTIVE STALE-LAW CORRECTION and is governed separately from the caveat-closure record, exactly as section 4 of the brief requires.

authority.how_read: The Act's text layer was extracted in full: 118 pages, 393,583 characters. Every section cited below was resolved and read directly from that text and occurs exactly once as an operative section. Pass 2A's mapping was treated as an AUTHORISATION, not as evidence, and independently re-verified before anything was written candidate-facing.
authority.extraction_hazards: TWO, recorded because one produced a false negative. (1) The Act's PDF separates a section number from its text with a 0x03 CONTROL BYTE as well as with a space, so a '^[0-9]+[.]\s' scan under-reports: s.319 was reported NOT FOUND on the first pass and is present exactly as authorised. A negative from a text scan is only evidence once the scan is proved able to find a positive. (2) The s.281(2) penalty table renumbers its rows 1..N, so a naive scan resolves 'section 15' to a table row about s.139; table rows must be excluded before a section number is resolved.
authority.part_structure: Verified from the Act: I ss.1-3; II ss.4-13; III ss.14-44; IV ss.45-53; V ss.54-113; VI ss.114-130; VII ss.131-143; VIII ss.144-152; IX ss.153-222; X ss.223-230; XI ss.231-232; XII ss.233-260; XIII ss.261-280; XIV ss.281-292; XV ss.293-324; XVI s.325.
authority.the_negative: Whole-document search of the held PDF: the expression 'formal investigation' occurs ZERO times in the Merchant Shipping Act 2025. The 1958 framework's preliminary-inquiry / formal-investigation pairing is NOT carried forward under that name.
authority.part_xi_is_two_sections: Part XI, 'INVESTIGATION AND INQUIRIES ON MARINE CASUALTIES', is ss.231-232 and nothing else - Part XII begins at s.233. The authorisation's 'Part XI - ss.231-232' is exact.
authority.the_four_steps: s.231(2): the ship owner, manager, operator, company, pilot, harbour master, master or other person in charge shall, WITHIN TWENTY-FOUR HOURS of the occurrence, give notice of the marine casualty to the officer appointed in this behalf by the Central Government. s.231(3)-(4): that officer shall forthwith inform the Central Government in writing and proceed to make a PRELIMINARY INQUIRY, furnishing his report on completion. s.231(5)-(6): the Central Government may appoint a body to conduct a MARINE SAFETY INVESTIGATION in accordance with the Safety Convention; it makes a preliminary assessment, ascertains causes and circumstances and submits its report. s.232: on that report, or on a prima facie view of incompetency, misconduct or violation of law, the Central Government may (a) initiate administrative action and (b) direct the authority having jurisdiction to initiate proceedings.
authority.certificates_are_separate: The power over an officer's certificate that the old 'formal investigation' carried is NOT an output of the s.231 machinery. It is s.312, in Part XV: the Central Government may by order cancel or suspend a certificate where an inquiry or investigation report reveals incompetency or misconduct, on failure to render assistance after a collision, on conviction, where a casualty was caused by wrongful act or default, or on contravention of the Act.
authority.definitions_boundary: s.231(1)(a)-(g) deems what is a marine casualty FOR PART XI. s.224(a) separately defines 'marine incident' FOR PART X. AND THE BOUNDARY THAT MATTERS: the phrase 'very serious marine casualty' occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the entire Act, inside the s.224(a) inclusion list. The Act NAMES the term and does NOT DEFINE it; the definition remains Casualty Investigation Code MSC.255(84) terminology. Both 'the Act defines very serious marine casualty' and 'the term does not appear in the Act' are FALSE, and only reading the provision produces the true, narrower claim now on the card.
authority.restructure_not_renumbering: oralnotes/miw-notes-mgmt-p15 described the change as a '2025 renumbering'. It is a RESTRUCTURE: a limb was dropped, not renumbered. A consolidating statute may only be called a renumbering when the limbs actually survive.
